title: The strategy behind the work.
intro: Selected Ardiles work in consumer insight, category positioning, product communication, launch preparation, and marketing operations.

cases.title: Consumer insight & brand direction
cases.summary: Connecting consumer needs with a clear Performance brand direction and distinct Running and Basketball communication.
cases.challenge: Build a shared brand direction while giving Running and Basketball clear roles for different consumers, use cases, and sporting contexts.
cases.role: Worked on research interpretation, category positioning, audience frameworks, and communication direction within the Ardiles brand team.

proof.label: respondents in the directional JAKPAT study
proof.note: A non-probability panel sample. Findings describe the reviewed sample; the later questionnaire is a separate piece of work.

modules.title: Consumer research & quality checks
modules.text: Reviewed purchase priorities, barriers among aware non-buyers, response quality, and question denominators. Fit and feel formed the leading pair of purchase priorities; awareness, design relevance, and brand loyalty were important barriers in the non-buyer group.

modules.title: One brand, two sport contexts
modules.text: Developed category communication around progress, training, and learning for Running, and expression, play, style, and crew culture for Basketball. Kept the shared brand foundation distinct from seasonal campaign treatments.

modules.title: Questionnaire design
modules.text: Refined purchase-and-usage questions, separated wearer, chooser, and payer roles, and developed relevant Running and Basketball paths. The questionnaire starts with actual needs and purchases before hypothetical preferences.

cases.deliverable: Research readouts, category positioning and audience frameworks, communication principles, and a branching customer questionnaire.

cases.title: Product messaging & SS27 launch preparation
cases.summary: Making product roles and technical information easier to explain across customer, retailer, media, and event communication.
cases.challenge: Connect product information, consumer relevance, and launch storytelling without treating a technology name as proof of a benefit.
cases.role: Translated supplied product and research material into marketing copy, developed launch narratives and editor guidance, and prepared retailer and media communication.

proof.label: technology-description cells revised
proof.note: Saved revision in the Running 2027 copy sheet, 25 October 2026. Word counts include technology headings. This measures the copy revision, not sales or comprehension improvement.

modules.title: Product roles & differentiation
modules.text: Refined Daywalker’s walking-led message, with easy running as the secondary context, and reviewed the distinct reasons to choose products in the Drive range. Shared technology names were kept separate from meaningful product differentiation.

modules.title: Product communication standards
modules.text: Simplified and aligned upper, insole, plate, midsole, outsole, and Gerbera upgrade descriptions while retaining names, component details, and intended use. Reduced the reviewed text from 1,158 to 753 words.

modules.title: SS27 narrative & creative direction
modules.text: Developed brand-story and Performance-film materials, storyboards, scene mapping, footage references, and editor explanations. Prepared presentation narratives, media Q&A, and MC talking points for the collection launch.

modules.title: Retailer experience & enablement
modules.text: Proposed guided fitting and product-understanding experiences for different retail audiences, connecting model selection and fit/feel with assortment and ordering conversations.

modules.title: Research communication
modules.text: Prepared communication around the Drive Revounce pilot with UNESA, keeping product, comparison, sample, and measurement context explicit. This work concerns research interpretation and messaging.

modules.title: Futsal & Soccer communication
modules.text: Prepared category-entry messaging and product-use-case descriptions from supplied engineering material, including construction, component roles, and intended playing context.

cases.deliverable: A saved product-copy revision, product-role work, launch narratives, creative briefs, retailer-experience concepts, presentation materials, and media and event copy. Planning and draft materials are identified above.

cases.title: Budgets, sponsorships & partner programs
cases.summary: Giving marketing investments and partnerships a clearer scope, review structure, and set of deliverables.
cases.challenge: Make spending, partner responsibilities, content delivery, and the value of support clear enough to review before and during campaigns.
cases.role: Worked on budget reconciliation, sponsorship criteria, market and audience reporting, retailer participation, content planning, and affiliate-program materials.

proof.label: transaction records in the Q3 budget reconciliation
proof.note: The count describes workbook-review scope. Cut-off and source differences were identified for follow-up; no cost-saving amount is claimed.

modules.title: Budget review & variance tracking
modules.text: Reviewed transaction dates, amounts, category mappings, monthly usage, and remaining budgets across Running and Basketball. Kept KOL and Seeding separate and identified differences between reporting sources and cut-off dates.

modules.title: Market & audience intelligence
modules.text: Prepared a regional review of online commercial signals and social audiences for Jabodetabek, with explicit periods, denominators, regional comparisons, and coverage limits.

modules.title: Sponsorship evaluation framework
modules.text: Developed a coded assessment and agreement format covering product trials, feedback, prizes, asset delivery, deadlines, and usage permissions, with Continue, Negotiate, and Reject review states.

modules.title: Retail-partner marketing
modules.text: Developed Runergize Showdown participation mechanics and content briefs for partner stores, connecting a product campaign with retailer-created communication and defined content-use terms.

modules.title: Event-to-content planning
modules.text: Planned participant experience content, primary interviews, later reviews, deliverables, and reuse requirements for Run Into the Wild. The playbook’s planned output is separate from completed delivery.

modules.title: Affiliate-program design
modules.text: Prepared recruitment presentations, reward structures, sample rules, and benefit summaries for review with the commercial terms owner.

modules.title: Digital-commerce diagnostics
modules.text: Reviewed TikTok purchase-information gaps and website SEO foundations, then outlined measurement and testing priorities. These diagnostic outputs do not establish subsequent traffic or sales uplift.

cases.deliverable: Budget-review workbooks, a published regional report, a sponsorship assessment draft, retailer challenge briefs, an event-content playbook, affiliate-program drafts, and diagnostic recommendations.

connections.title: Research, product marketing & operations
connections.text: Consumer research, category positioning, product messaging, and operating frameworks form part of the strategic work behind these campaigns.

connections.title: Launch planning & communication
connections.text: The wider campaign work included phased communication, creator briefs, PR drafts, educational content, and event-documentation requirements.

connections.title: Product-role thinking
connections.text: The creative direction prioritised walking and everyday use, with easy running as a secondary context. Product-role work separated the intended use case from shared technology names.

connections.title: Runergize Showdown: retail-partner marketing
connections.text: The campaign design included a structured content challenge for partner stores, with participation requirements, posting mechanics, timing, and content-use terms.

connections.title: Event-to-content planning
connections.text: A participant-content playbook planned experience posts, interviews, follow-up reviews, deliverables, and asset reuse alongside the event communication.
